text: You never put a shed straight on grass.
First, a layer of hardcore, packed down hard, then sand, then paving slabs, perfectly level.
Timber bearers lift the floor off the slabs, so air flows underneath and the damp stays out.
Then the walls, and a roof. Your shed is done.
But the lawnmower doesn't fit. So you add an extension.
Then the bikes don't fit. So you add a second floor.
The stairs take up all the room. So you bolt a lift to the outside.
The lift needs power. So you cover the roof in solar panels.
But next door's tree shades the panels. So you build above the tree.
Higher means a longer lift. A longer lift needs more panels. More panels need more roof.
Congratulations. You own the tallest shed in the country. And you still can't find the screwdriver.
